assessment.overall_rationale: The sets closely correspond at all three biological levels: pathway execution, sterol-sensing transcriptional control, and coupling of cholesterol synthesis to hepatic lipid supply and export.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe essentially the same near-complete enzymatic mevalonate-to-cholesterol cascade in hepatocytes, with only minor differences in substrate supply and cholesterol esterification details.
Both concern hepatic cholesterol synthesis, but the left module is the enzymatic pathway whereas the right module centers on SREBP2-dependent transcriptional control.

They overlap through ACSS2-supported cholesterol synthesis and hepatic lipid metabolism, but the right module emphasizes substrate provision, triglyceride handling, and VLDL export rather than the sterol enzyme cascade.
The modules address the same cholesterol program, but the left specifies its SCAP–INSIG1–SREBP2 regulatory circuit while the right describes the downstream biosynthetic enzymes.
Both describe SCAP–INSIG1-dependent SREBP2 activation, LDLR-linked feedback, and transcriptional regulation of hepatic cholesterol homeostasis with matching functional direction.
Both link regulatory perturbations to hepatic cholesterol homeostasis, but sterol-sensing transcriptional feedback is mechanistically distinct from acetyl-CoA supply and lipoprotein assembly.
Both concern hepatic cholesterol production, but VLDL-triglyceride export coupling is distinct from the downstream enzymatic sterol biosynthesis cascade.
They share coordinated hepatic cholesterol homeostasis and MASLD context, but lipid export control and SREBP2 sterol sensing are different central mechanisms.
Both connect ACSS2-derived substrate supply and DGAT2–MTTP-mediated triglyceride/VLDL handling to hepatic cholesterol synthesis and export, with the right adding mechanistic detail on ACAT2 coupling.
